summary.text: Repeated failed sign-ins for user-01 from ip-01 were followed by a successful sign-in, an encoded PowerShell launch on host-02, an SMB logon and a new service on host-03, a large file read on host-03 and a 480 MB transfer from ip-02 to ip-04.

claim.text: The events match password guessing followed by movement to a file server and a large outbound transfer.

sequence.text: Five failed sign-ins for user-01 from ip-01 on host-01 within 24 seconds.
A successful sign-in for user-01 from ip-01.
An encoded PowerShell command ran on host-02 under user-01.
An SMB logon to host-03 as user-01, then creation of the service 'updsvc'.
user-01 read 1,812 files under /finance/archive on host-03, then ip-02 sent 480 MB to ip-04 over TCP 443.

findings.text: A burst of failed sign-ins from one source followed by a success is consistent with password guessing against user-01.
PowerShell with an encoded command ran on host-02 under user-01 seven minutes after the successful sign-in.
The new service 'updsvc' on host-03 shortly after a remote logon may be a persistence step.

impact.text: Data from /finance/archive on host-03 may have left the network: 480 MB was sent from ip-02 to ip-04.

recommendations.action: Review the recent activity of user-01 and consider resetting its credentials.
recommendations.rationale: The account signed in after repeated failures and was then used on two more hosts.
recommendations.reversible_alternative: Require re-authentication at the next sign-in instead of a reset.

recommendations.action: Inspect the service 'updsvc' on host-03, its binary and who created it.
recommendations.rationale: It was created right after the SMB logon.

recommendations.action: Review the outbound transfer to ip-04 and the files read from /finance/archive.
recommendations.rationale: A 480 MB transfer followed a large file read on the same server.
recommendations.reversible_alternative: Alert on further traffic to ip-04 before blocking it.

risk_justification.text: The given High score fits a successful sign-in after repeated failures, use of the account on a second and third host, and a large outbound transfer from a file server.

uncertainties.statement: The events do not show what the encoded PowerShell command did.
uncertainties.missing_evidence: Script block or command-line logging on host-02.

uncertainties.statement: The events do not show that the transferred data is the data that was read.
uncertainties.missing_evidence: File access and flow logs with file names or hashes on host-03.

uncertainties.statement: One context event contains text that tries to give instructions; it was treated as data.
uncertainties.missing_evidence: None; it does not change the analysis.

limitations: Host, IP and user values are pseudonymised tokens, so ownership and location of the hosts are unknown.
Only 13 events from five log sources were available.
